title: After resume from sleep with different monitor configuration, Plasmashell crashed in KConfigGroup::config while trying to look up panel thickness
line: Plasma no longer crashes when a script reads the settings of a panel whose monitor was unplugged.
explanation: A panel whose monitor is gone has no view, so the scripting Panel object reads its settings from config. It looked the config group up through the panel's screen, and when that screen no longer existed (the size check was also off by one) it got an invalid KConfigGroup, and readEntry("thickness") on it dereferenced a null pointer. Anything calling PlasmaShell.evaluateScript on resume, like the reporter's setup, crashed plasmashell. The change reads and writes the panel's own Defaults group and its parent directly, which never depend on a screen.

commits.message:
shell/scripting: don't crash reading a panel whose screen is gone

Reading a panel property such as height from a script crashed
plasmashell when the panel's screen was gone, as the config lookup went
through the missing screen. Now it uses the panel's own config groups.

BUG: 524224

media.caption: Master: with the panel's monitor unplugged, a script reading panel height crashes plasmashell (gdb: Panel::height -> readEntry("thickness") on an invalid group)
With the fix: the same script returns values for both panels and plasmashell keeps running; settings written meanwhile apply on replug

review.text: This fixes the real cause: scripting Panel looked up the config through screenForId() of a screen that no longer exists, then read from an invalid group. The Defaults group and its parent don't depend on a screen, so dropping the screen parameter is the simple and correct fix. It also makes PanelView::configDefaults() valid for a viewless panel. The small behaviour change (a viewless panel without a Defaults group reports height 0 instead of a per-resolution value) is acceptable compared with a crash.
